overview: West Strand — also known as West Bay or Mill Strand — sits right in the middle of Portrush, with the harbour at its northern end and a pedestrian and cycle promenade running along its back. You can walk down from the town centre in minutes, which makes it the easiest beach on the coast to combine with lunch, a wander round the shops or an evening out. It holds Blue Flag status, most recently in 2024.

The beach has a story under the sand. The council notes it is protected as an Area of Special Scientific Interest because of buried peat beds and ancient sands, which hold fossil remains of alder and birch trees from roughly 9,000 to 7,000 years ago. Keep watching the water too: a resident pod of harbour porpoises is often seen just offshore.

For surfers it is a handy alternative to East Strand, facing a slightly different direction, so it is always worth comparing the two before you change. Lifeguards patrol in July and August. Facilities are mostly in town rather than on the sand, and the beach is narrower than its eastern neighbour, so it can feel cramped on a busy high tide in summer.

text: West Strand is a sandy beach break with lefts and rights. Like the rest of the Portrush coast it relies on north-westerly swell, and summer is often small or flat. Because it faces a different way from East Strand, one beach can be cleaner than the other on the same day, so check both before you commit.

The harbour wall at the northern end, swimmers close to the promenade and a narrowing beach at high tide all need care. Stay inside the black-and-white flagged zone for boards when lifeguards are on duty, and keep clear of harbour traffic.

West Strand faces north-west, so it takes the same swell as East Strand and works from around 2ft up to about 8ft before it gets too big. The bank is usually most consistent on a rising tide, though it works at every stage, and a south-easterly wind blows it offshore. Spring, especially April, shows up as the cleanest month in forecast data, and summer is often flat.

As the beach in the middle of town, with a surf school on the sand, a lifeguard in season and a surf shop close by, it's busy, especially in summer. If it's small and crowded here, check East Strand along the coast, which is bigger and usually has more space.

cards.title: Beginners to intermediates

cards.label: Conditions
cards.title: NW swell, rising tide
cards.text: 2 to 8ft is the usable range; a south-easterly wind is offshore.

cards.label: Season
cards.title: Spring
cards.text: April is the cleanest month in forecast data; summer is often flat and busy.

cards.label: Hazards
cards.title: Harbour and crowds
cards.text: Harbour structures, swimmers and a narrow high-tide beach.

practical.label: Parking
practical.title: Seasonal charges
practical.text: Parking is charged from 1 April to 30 September. Accessible parking and cycle parking are available.

practical.label: Facilities
practical.title: Town on the doorstep
practical.text: Accessible toilets, plus cafés, restaurants, shops and amusements behind the promenade.

practical.label: Lifeguards
practical.title: Seasonal RNLI patrol
practical.text: The council lists a seasonal RNLI patrol, 10am–6pm daily in July and August. Check the RNLI site for this year's dates.

practical.label: Dogs
practical.title: Summer restrictions
practical.text: The council allows dogs but applies restrictions from 1 June to 15 September — check the signs at the entrance for where they apply.

practical.label: Getting here
practical.title: Walk from the station
practical.text: Portrush railway station is a short walk away through the town.

faqs.q: Is West Strand the same as West Bay?
faqs.a: Yes. It is also called West Bay or Mill Strand.
The council lists a seasonal RNLI patrol, 10am–6pm daily in July and August.
The council says a resident pod of harbour porpoises can be seen just off the shore.
